questions.prompt: A walker moves \(5\) m east then \(2\) m east. Find the resultant displacement.
questions.answer: Same-direction displacements add: \(5+2=7\) m east.

questions.prompt: Compute \(3\mathbf i-2\mathbf j+(-5\mathbf i+7\mathbf j)\).
questions.answer: Collect components: \((3-5)\mathbf i+(-2+7)\mathbf j=-2\mathbf i+5\mathbf j\).

questions.prompt: A boat travels \(4\) km north then \(3\) km east. Write the resultant vector and magnitude.
questions.answer: The vector is \(3\mathbf i+4\mathbf j\) km. Its magnitude is \(5\) km by \(\sqrt{3^2+4^2}\).
Add components: \((7,-4,-3)\).

questions.prompt: Find \(\overrightarrow{AC}\) if \(\overrightarrow{AB}=(3,4)\) and \(\overrightarrow{BC}=(3,-5)\).
questions.answer: Use head-to-tail addition: \(\overrightarrow{AC}=\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{BC}=(6,-1)\).

questions.prompt: Three forces are \((2,1)\) N, \((-5,3)\) N, and \((4,-6)\) N. Find the resultant.
A drone moves \((1,2,0)\) m, then \((0,-3,4)\) m. Find final displacement from the start.
Find \(\mathbf a+\mathbf b\) and its magnitude for \(\mathbf a=(6,2)\), \(\mathbf b=(-1,10)\).
questions.answer: The sum is \((5,12)\). Its magnitude is \(\sqrt{25+144}=13\).

questions.prompt: Find \(\mathbf x\) if \(\mathbf x+(2,-7)=(5,1)\).
A hiker walks \(6\) km east, \(2\) km south, then \(1\) km west. Find resultant vector and magnitude.
questions.answer: The vector is \((6,0)+(0,-2)+(-1,0)=(5,-2)\) km. Its magnitude is \(\sqrt{29}\) km.

questions.prompt: Compute \(\mathbf p+\mathbf q+\mathbf r\) for \(\mathbf p=(2,-1,3)\), \(\mathbf q=(-4,5,0)\), \(\mathbf r=(1,1,-6)\).
Given \(\overrightarrow{AB}=(4,-2)\) and \(\overrightarrow{AC}=(1,5)\), find \(\overrightarrow{BC}\).
questions.answer: Since \(\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{BC}=\overrightarrow{AC}\), \(\overrightarrow{BC}=(1,5)-(4,-2)=(-3,7)\).

questions.prompt: Two tugs pull with forces \(8\) N east and \(6\) N north. Find resultant magnitude and direction north of east.
questions.answer: The resultant is \((8,6)\) N. Its magnitude is \(10\) N and \(\tan\theta=6/8\), so \(\theta\approx36.9^\circ\).

questions.prompt: A particle moves from \(A=(1,-2,3)\) to \(B=(4,0,-1)\), then to \(C=(-2,5,2)\). Find the resultant displacement and the total path length travelled.
questions.answer: First \(\overrightarrow{AB}=B-A=(3,2,-4)\) and \(\overrightarrow{BC}=C-B=(-6,5,3)\). The resultant is \(\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{BC}=(-3,7,-1)\), which also equals \(C-A\). The path length is \(|\overrightarrow{AB}|+|\overrightarrow{BC}|=\sqrt{3^2+2^2+(-4)^2}+\sqrt{(-6)^2+5^2+3^2}=\sqrt{29}+\sqrt{70}\).

questions.prompt: Three coplanar forces keep a joint in equilibrium. Two forces are \((3,-8)\) N and \((-1,5)\) N. Find the third force and its magnitude.
questions.answer: Equilibrium means the total force is \(\mathbf0\). The two known forces sum to \((3-1,-8+5)=(2,-3)\) N, so the third force is \((-2,3)\) N. Its magnitude is \(\sqrt{(-2)^2+3^2}=\sqrt{13}\) N.

questions.prompt: A drone starts at \((2,1,5)\), makes displacements \((-4,3,2)\) and \((1,-6,-7)\), then must end at \((0,0,4)\). Find the final correction displacement.
questions.answer: The first two displacements sum to \((-3,-3,-5)\), so the intermediate position is \((2,1,5)+(-3,-3,-5)=(-1,-2,0)\). To end at \((0,0,4)\), the correction is \((0,0,4)-(-1,-2,0)=(1,2,4)\).

questions.prompt: A robot starts at \((1,2)\), moves by \(2\mathbf i-\mathbf j\), then by \(-3\mathbf i+4\mathbf j\), then by \(\mathbf i-6\mathbf j\). Find its final position and the single displacement that would return it to the start.
questions.answer: The total movement is \((2,-1)+(-3,4)+(1,-6)=(0,-3)\). The final position is \((1,2)+(0,-3)=(1,-1)\). To return to the start, the robot needs the opposite displacement \((0,3)=3\mathbf j\).

questions.prompt: Air velocity is \((90,0)\) km h\(^{-1}\) and wind velocity is \((-20,15)\) km h\(^{-1}\). Find ground velocity and speed.
Four displacement vectors form a closed path: \((2,5)\), \((-1,3)\), \((4,-6)\), and \(\mathbf d\). Find \(\mathbf d\).
questions.answer: The first three sum to \((5,2)\). A closed path has total \((0,0)\), so \(\mathbf d=(-5,-2)\).
